THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1.
Heard learned counsel for petitioner, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1-State and learned counsel for respondent No.2 - complainant.

2. Accused No.1 has filed this petition under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., praying to grant bail in Spl.C.
POCSO No.12/2023 on the file of the Additional District NC: 2023:KHC-K:6522 and Sessions Judge, FTSC-I Special Court for POCSO at Kalaburagi, seeking to release him on bail.

entities.text: Sessions Judge, FTSC-I Special Court for POCSO at Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. The brief facts of the prosecution case are as under:
On 10.12.2022 victim lodged a complaint against petitioner and another alleging that she was studying in VIII Std., in Government High School at Yadga Village, Sedam Taluk, Kalaburagi District and she used to go to her School from Bibballi Village by walk and the accused persons used to see her and follow her wherever she goes.

On 01.11.2022 she had been to School and after celebration of 'Karnataka Rajyothasava',
she came out of her School at 2:00 p.m., at that time accused No.2 came there on his motorcycle and asked victim to accompany him in his motorcycle, with an assurance to drop her home.

He took victim on his motorcycle and dropped her near Boothpura Sudhakar vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101452881/
2 Cross where accused No.1 - petitioner was standing.

entities.text: Boothpura Sudhakar vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When victim alighted motorcycle of accused NC: 2023:KHC-K:6522 No.2, petitioner holding hands of victim took her to the land situated by the side of road, dragged her and touched her body, at that time victim escaped from the clutches of petitioner and ran away towards main road.
At that time one motorcycle came on main road, she requested the rider of the motorcycle to drop her to her village.
Thus the said motorcyclist dropped her to her home.

After 5-6 days of the incident, victim had been to attend nature call, at that time petitioner followed her, took her to sugarcane field and removed her clothes and committed sexual intercourse on her forcibly and later he gave threat of eliminating her if she reveals the said fact to her parents.

Hence, after 40 days of the incident she lodged complaint and thus, respondent-Police registered a case in Crime No.61/2022 for the offences punishable under Sections 354(A), 376 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 6, 8 and 12 of POCSO Act, 2012.
During the course of investigation the accused were arrested and in turn remanded to judicial custody.

Petitioner filed bail petition in Crl.Misc. No.997/2023 before the trial Court and the NC:
2023:KHC-K:6522 trial Court rejected his bail petition on 24.06.2023.

Hence,
petitioner filed the instant petition.
4. It is contended that the allegations made against petitioner are false.

There is inordinate delay of 40 days in lodging FIR and no proper explanation has been offered by the first informant; petitioner is aged about 19 years and he is in judicial custody since 11.12.2022 and he is the only bread earner in his family; he is ready to abide by any conditions to be imposed by this Court.
5. Learned High Court Government Pleader contended that petitioner has committed a serious offence of sexual assault on a minor girl, hence there is prima facie case against him.
If petitioner is released on bail, he may tamper the prosecution witnesses, he may influence the victim and there is likelihood of he fleeing away from justice.

6. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 contended that petitioner - accused No.1 has involved in a serious NC: 2023:KHC-K:6522 offence, the victim has clearly stated against petitioner before the learned magistrate under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., as well as before the trial Court on oath.
As per medical evidence, her hymen was ruptured.
Now the matter is set down for trial and if petitioner is released on bail he may tamper the remaining prosecution witnesses.
On all these grounds he prayed to reject the petition.

In support of his contention, the learned counsel has relied upon the following decisions of this Court:
1. Crl. Petition No.1251/2020 - Krishna R. vs. State of Karnataka 2.

sentences.text: I have perused the grounds urged in the bail petition, FIR, complaint, charge sheet and other materials NC: 2023:KHC-K:6522 produced in this case.
On perusal of the material available on record, it appears that the date of birth of victim is 09.04.2009 and the date of incident is 01.11.2022.
Thus, as on the date of incident, victim was aged about 13 years 5 months.
On perusal of the statement of victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., it reveals that petitioner forcibly took victim to the sugarcane land and committed aggravated sexual assault on her.

8. In the statement made by the victim girl under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C., as well as in her evidence on oath, no where she had admitted that, she gave consent or she was willing to have such sexual intercourse with the petitioner.
Even in the complaint, statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., and in the evidence, she has stated that, it was forcibly sexual intercourse on her.

No doubt,
there is delay of forty days in lodging the complaint, but victim has properly explained the delay, as there was threat by petitioner.
On perusal of the Medical records, the hymen is ruptured.

It is true that, medical records will not support the prosecution case, but it may not be accepted by the Court that after 40 days of the incident, there can be supportive medical records regarding seminal stain and also injury to the private parts, etc.
10.
Admittedly, the victim is minor, the question of consent would not arise in an allegation of aggravated sexual assault under POCSO Act.

11. Having regard to the materials placed on record, the victim girl is below 14 years, the prosecution has placed prima facie materials to prove the involvement of the petitioner in committing alleged offences which attracts the provision of POCSO Act.
Now the trial is pending before the trial Court and evidence of PWs.1 to 5 have been recorded and the remaining witnesses are required to be examined yet.
If petitioner is released on bail, he may threaten the prosecution witnesses and may NC: 2023:KHC-K:6522 hamper the trial.
Therefore, considering all these aspects of the matter, it is not a case for grant of bail.
Accordingly, the petition is rejected.
